name: Nick Baltas
one_paragraph: Baltas is a quant/QIS strategist who thinks of trend following as a rules-based, permanent, never-timed way to be positioned for sustained moves and prolonged drawdowns (trend earns when information is digested gradually and fundamentals are uncertain; it does not earn in short V-shaped spike-and-revert events, which hit the medium speeds twice and are the main cause of manager dispersion). He makes his case from first principles and from papers he reads closely (Man Group, Quantica, ATP, Graham, AQR, Harvey et al.) plus his own year-by-year speed/universe grids and attribution, and he flags hunches, hindsight bias and data mining himself. His working rules: scale every exposure by volatility (and correlation), let risk flow to where trends exist, keep a broad 50-100 market universe without screening out past losers, add beta-neutral carry and reversion to diversify the periods when trend fails, match universe and speed to the objective (core liquid markets for crisis alpha, broad for long-run Sharpe), size the allocation by tracking error against the policy benchmark rather than by optimiser, never change a model because of one episode or one year's ranking, and treat crowding as a question of whether the return is a genuine risk premium (survives, only varies) or a flow imbalance (erodes). Money is made by harvesting a small number of durable premia (trend, carry, reversion/skew, vol selling) in diversified, volatility-controlled form and by staying invested through known losing regimes; he does not forecast markets and says even reading the current state is hard.

core_beliefs.belief: V-shaped spike-and-revert events (Volmageddon, SVB, Aug 2024, Apr 2025, Mar 2026) are an expected cost of trend following, not a break in it: a V is two reversals in a row, no speed escapes, the medium speeds (3-6 months) are caught both ways, and they are the main source of manager dispersion.
core_beliefs.stable: stable - same V-shape logic from Aug 2024 to Mar 2026; added nuance 2026: the March 2026 V (slow drop, fast recovery) hurt trend less and faster speeds beat slower (MT167-C06-1, MT174-C05-2)

core_beliefs.belief: Trend pays in sustained equity/bond drawdowns and inflation-shock years (2002, 2008, 2022), not in short V-shaped drops; trend followers are price takers, not forecasters, and do not earn in the months before an equity peak or the first weeks after it starts.

Do not change a trend model (speed, universe, vol target) because of one episode, one painful year or one year's ranking: leadership rotates, such findings are data mining or false positives, and pain is an invitation to review blind spots, not to change.
core_beliefs.stable: stable in words; evolved in practice at the margin - in June 2025 he floated a lower or dynamic vol target after repeated V-shapes while admitting hindsight bias (MT087-C08-2, MT087-C08-X1)

core_beliefs.belief: Trend following should be a permanent, strategic, never-timed allocation (insurance-like, sized and left alone); past performance weakly predicts future returns and outperformance often begins after underperformance; regime timing of trend is unproven.

Choose the market universe and speed by the objective: a small core liquid universe (equity, duration principal components) maximises crisis alpha and defensiveness; a broad 50-100+ universe (with commodities) maximises long-run Sharpe; beyond 70-80 liquid macro markets nothing new is added, exotic commodities still add return.
core_beliefs.stable: stable; 2024 statement on 'no sweet spot of speed' becomes 2026 'objective decides'

core_beliefs.belief: Breadth without performance screening is how trend earns its keep: markets that were historically the worst contributors (cocoa) can become the big winners, and one cannot forecast which markets will trend; select markets for diversification and cost, not past contribution.

Risk is forecastable but returns are not: scale every exposure by volatility (and by correlation, if not too noisy) rather than by fixed budgets, which embed hidden return forecasts and a value bet; a fixed risk budget forces capital into non-trending markets.
core_beliefs.stable: evolved - May 2024 / Aug 2024 he personally prefers dynamic allocation across asset classes (MT117-C09-1, MT099-C08-R3); by Oct 2024 he notes static and dynamic converge long-run and matter locally at turning points (MT200-C10-2); June 2025 he considers a lower, time-varying vol target (MT087-C08-2)

core_beliefs.belief: Diversify trend with non-trend premia - beta-neutral/cross-sectional carry, reversion (skew-based), vol selling, economic/macro trend - because trend already carries equity beta and fails in V-shapes; non-trend sleeves also keep loss-averse investors allocated.

What matters for crowding is the type of return: a genuine risk premium (vol selling, curve carry) keeps a non-negative expected reward even when crowded (size and timing vary); an arbitrage-like flow imbalance (roll-window congestion) is eroded by capital; behavioural premia (trend) may benefit from early crowding; the real risk is shared-signal externalities and forced liquidation, which cannot be quantified.
core_beliefs.stable: stable framework; tone varies - dismisses blame on CTAs/vol targeters as unsupported (MT002, MT099) but asks for conservative design because externalities are unquantifiable (MT216)

core_beliefs.belief: Trend works because information is digested slowly and because fundamentals are uncertain/disputed (price moves carry information) and volatility clusters (predictability without serial correlation); it fails under fundamental certainty (Fed put era, consensus valuation) where shocks revert.

Allocation size is set by institutional constraints, not optimisation: mean-variance gives ~70% and downside-risk ~52% in trend, which is unusable; benchmarked allocators face tracking-error and career risk, so size by scenario analysis against the policy portfolio (sleeves of 2-15%, ideally 5-20% in the strategic benchmark). Many alternative-asset returns and anomalies come from such constraints.
Investors are loss-averse, so drawdowns drive behaviour (cutting allocations, chasing the last defensive product that worked); paying a long-run premium for downside protection can be rational.

Risk is measurable, uncertainty is not; even identifying the current market state is hard, consensus forecasts fail, and portfolios should allow for the unseen (diversify more and rely less on return forecasts when the regime is unclear).

Defence should be layered because each hedge covers a different drawdown type: options/short delta for flash corrections, trend for prolonged drawdowns and stock-bond correlation (inflation) shocks, and a non-short-gamma diversifying bucket (curve carry, ARP) to offset the carry cost; safe equities are only a relative defence.

Themes and narratives are a tagging layer without a risk premium that raise within-theme correlation and can lead price momentum; they help discretionary investors with limited attention more than systematic ones; he is exploring narrative data but has no result.
core_beliefs.stable: evolved - Jan 2026 'experiment, no answer' (MT116-C03-2); Jul 2026 more developed (narrative beta, evergreen topics) but second-hand from papers he did not write (MT174-C16-1)

core_beliefs.belief: AI/LLMs are a large efficiency tool for research and coding but need human framing and checking: LLMs fabricated references and gave wrong CTA numbers, agentic backtests suffer look-ahead, non-reproducibility and monoculture.
core_beliefs.stable: evolved - mid-2025 verify LLM output after hallucination (MT087-C02-1); Mar 2026 task-specific agents inside a deterministic pipeline under supervision (MT167-C14-X10); Jul 2026 uses a daily agent but checks numbers (MT174-C03-2)

core_beliefs.belief: An index/benchmark like SG Trend is realised returns of evolving real programs (beta plus or minus alpha, survivorship-shaped), so rising correlation to it cannot prove CTAs 'slowed'; signal forms are transformations of each other, so effort belongs in portfolio construction and risk management; research mostly changes risk management, not speed.

Data mining is unavoidable and is controlled by culture and by explaining performance (changes justified by explanation, not repair after a drawdown); a premium should be retired only when its underlying economic reason has changed, not on statistics.

mechanisms.name: V-shape hits trend twice, middle speeds worst
chain: Sharp fall (or rally) -> signals need days to cut/flip, so medium-speed models are short near the trough (positions lag price)
Rebound -> models re-add into it or reversion arrives as they reposition; both legs are late (resonance, 'soldiers on a bridge')
Fast signals lose less on the way down but recover less; slow signals ride the whole V; all end negative, spread depends on speed
Synchronous reversion across equities, dollar, oil, yields -> no sector cushion
mechanisms.fails_when: Move becomes a sustained drawdown (2002, 2008, 2022): positions flip and earn; a real turn (true positive) favours fast signals; regime flips - March 2026 fast recovery V hurt trend less and faster beat slower

mechanisms.name: Trend does not earn before/after an equity peak
chain: Equities rally -> trend long, price taker
Sharp fall -> positions flip slowly, no gain in first weeks to a month
Three months before the peak other trends cease/re-establish -> reshuffling, no significant performance
Drawdown continues deeper/longer -> performance appears (dotcom, GFC, 2022)
mechanisms.fails_when: Equity decline is a V that reverses before positions flip (Volmageddon, SVB, Aug 2024, Apr 2025)

mechanisms.name: Leverage into unpredictable turning points sets the loss
chain: Turning points are not predictable
Realised vol = function of leverage = function of diversification/correlation (mixed positions need more leverage for a fixed vol target)
Twice the leverage, roughly twice the loss
Loss aversion -> preference for being under-levered in drawdown; possible lower/time-varying vol target
mechanisms.fails_when: If V-shapes are not more frequent, lowering leverage just gives up trend payoffs; rule fitted to the last drawdown; hindsight and path dependency; trendiness does not predict performance (only very high trendiness precedes weakness)

mechanisms.name: Fixed risk budgets embed return forecasts; correlation-aware dynamic budgets follow trend
chain: Fixed weights (60/40, equal risk per asset class) -> implied return forecast and value bet via rebalancing
Inverse-vol weights -> equal expected Sharpe assumed
Vol-only scaling -> correlated clusters over-represented
Dynamic budgets that follow trend strength -> capital goes where trends exist (rates ~10% of risk when not trending vs 25% balanced)
mechanisms.fails_when: Balanced allocation loses less in an equity reversal (equities caused 60% of Aug 2024 loss under dynamic allocation) - a trade-off between conviction and forced diversification; no backtest of fixed vs dynamic shown

mechanisms.name: Small signal differences make fragile relative-value positions
chain: Two 95%-correlated markets with signals 1 and 0.9 -> optimiser long stronger, short weaker
Spread has tiny risk -> grossed up to large leverage, apparent high Sharpe
Ordering reverses -> heavy loss on concentrated levered position
Middle ground: scale by signal strength / agnostic risk parity, no forced shorts
mechanisms.fails_when: Position depends entirely on forecast persistence and noise; no backtest shown

mechanisms.name: Why trend can work without serial correlation
chain: Consensus valuation (pre-2020) -> shocks are faded; inflation uncertainty (post-2020) widens views -> price moves carry information
Volatility clusters -> big moves followed by same-direction moves, skew without serial correlation
Conditional on a deep drawdown beyond a threshold, trend follower expects positive payoff (crisis alpha with iid returns, ATP paper)
Segregated commodity markets with persistent producer/speculator imbalance trend without high vol
mechanisms.fails_when: Fundamental certainty (Fed put 2010-2020) -> prices bounce back, trend weaker in rising equities

mechanisms.name: Equity momentum crowding: party and hangover
chain: Early crowding -> trade takes off
Buying winners raises prices, attracts more buying; indices concentrate; hedge funds hold record momentum exposure
FOMO and redemption risk keep momentum traders in despite known crash risk
Exit: funding liquidity/credit lines exhausted at max gross (endogenous) or idiosyncratic shock such as AI hype fading or value buyers (exogenous) -> fire sales, short squeezes
mechanisms.fails_when: Timing the end is very hard (he does not predict crashes); prudent response is volatility-scaling exposure

mechanisms.name: Correlation externalities and contagion in crowded trades
chain: Many investors hold similar leveraged portfolios (FX carry, 60/40 plus overlays) for similar objectives
Unrelated shock or VIX spike -> synchronous deleveraging, funding constraints, vicious circle
Backtested diversification overstates protection; allocators with same objective cut together and create correlation
mechanisms.fails_when: Not tested statistically; he asks for agent-level postmortem data

mechanisms.name: August 2024 yen-carry unwind to trend losses and dispersion
chain: BOJ hike + Fed cut expectations -> FX carry unwind; record-low equity correlations from mega-cap concentration + crowded short-vol/dispersion -> correlation spike, VIX 16 to 65
Trend long equities/short yen lose (equities 60% of loss for dynamic allocators); rates ~10% of risk
BOJ signals it will not hike -> V; VIX back to 24 within a week; SG Trend about -6% for the month, mostly reversing a prior gain
Dispersion by speed, equity caps, balanced vs dynamic allocation, number of markets, reversion/carry components
mechanisms.fails_when: In March 2023 the shock was in rates and hit all programs similarly regardless of design

mechanisms.name: Capping equity beta costs more than it saves
chain: Trend is net short equities in downturns -> CTAs positive in 12 of the worst 16 S&P quarters since 2000 (crisis beta plus crisis alpha)
Remove, cap or neutralise equity beta -> worst-quarter outcome improves only slightly (about 4.1% to 4.5-4.6%)
Costs about 200bp a year in the long run (Quantica); timing skill and bull-market participation lost
mechanisms.fails_when: Loss-averse investors may rationally pay the premium; if equity beta must be limited cap position-weighted market betas rather than short S&P futures

mechanisms.name: Carry inside a trend portfolio
chain: Time-series carry long positive-carry assets -> picks up beta (67% correlation of time-series bond carry to bond beta)
Oil in contango while price falls -> carry short profits from spot move = trend payoff
Neutralise beta -> mix of cross-sectional and time-series carry; design carry to minimise spot contribution
Carry filter on trend: no shorts in positively carrying assets, no longs in negative carry -> avoids pre-2022 carry drag
mechanisms.fails_when: Carry-optimised trend sample 1998-2023 coincides with the carry regime and may be overfit (host)

mechanisms.name: Commodity curve carry shock (2026) and recovery
chain: Long back, short front (roll yield) -> structurally short the front
Supply shock (Hormuz Mar 2026, Jan gas weather) -> backwardation, spot rally -> worst drawdown in 40 years (~10% simple implementation, ~2x 2018)
Backwardation mean-reverts unless supply shock permanent -> mark-to-market recovery
Beta-hedge the front, choose back dynamically or close spread in backwardation -> much smaller loss
mechanisms.fails_when: Supply shock is permanent; oil news-driven; closing spread gives up carry in backwardation

mechanisms.name: Crowding and premium type (roll congestion, vol selling)
chain: Passive index investors roll on predictable schedule -> pre-positioning earns liquidity premium (congestion)
Passive roll demand shrank -> market elastic, trade flattened 2015-19 (flat, not negative: not QIS crowding)
Demand returned after Russia-Ukraine -> trade back 2022
Risk-sharing premium: more sellers lower returns -> barrier to entry rises, premium stays positive
mechanisms.fails_when: Passive demand disappears, or QIS traders crowd into a pure flow imbalance; flows reverse after underperformance

mechanisms.name: Objective decides universe: principal components
chain: Crisis: correlations go to extremes, principal components (equity, duration) drive returns -> core liquid universe maximises crisis alpha and cash efficiency
Long-run Sharpe: more independent bets (alternative commodities, exotic markets) -> broader universe, less defensive
Extra markets in an already represented component only split a fixed risk budget; 60 equity factors are really 5-6
mechanisms.fails_when: One year (2026) of divergence between broad and concentrated books does not settle it

mechanisms.name: Dealer gamma and 0DTE options
chain: Customers sell options for carry -> dealers long gamma
Long gamma -> dealers buy dips, sell rallies -> intraday mean reversion; short gamma exacerbates trends
Possible drag on short-term trend; little effect on medium/long-term trend
mechanisms.fails_when: Not proven (cited with hedging; Vilkov et al.); no data that 0DTE drove August 2024

mechanisms.name: Theme-blind covariance misstates risk; narratives precede price
chain: Investors allocate by theme (AI, memory chips) -> within-theme correlation above sector links
Allocation into an inelastic market -> price pressure -> price path -> momentum models buy it
Covariance ignoring clusters understates risk; narrative life cycle (rise, peak, fade) gives measurable exposure beta
Demand/narrative precedes price momentum -> earlier signal
mechanisms.fails_when: Look-ahead from themes named only afterwards (shrinks with 30-60 evergreen topics); price, macro and thematic exposure are noisy transforms of one latent signal and agree in prolonged growth regimes

mechanisms.name: Short-term risk mitigation lifts long-term compounding
chain: Losses compound asymmetrically (10% loss needs ~11% gain)
Investor needs long-horizon return with short-horizon solvency checks -> downside-mitigating strategies valued even at similar arithmetic returns
Monte Carlo of 12-52 periods: compounded distribution shifts right; judge hedges in portfolio context like insurance (stand-alone negative expected return acceptable)
mechanisms.fails_when: Own Monte Carlo and rental-property analogy only

mechanisms.name: Scheduled rebalancing is front-run
chain: Fixed-weight 60/40 rebalances on a calendar (mechanically contrarian)
Fast money front-runs the flows: ~8bp a year on ~$20tn = ~$16bn (Harvey et al.)
Check the trend before rebalancing; avoid month/quarter ends; rebalance frequently with thresholds
mechanisms.fails_when: Estimate is third-party; trend persistence assumed

mechanisms.name: Trend sleeve as a hedge to a rate sell-off
chain: Rates reprice up (Sept 2026: 2-year +75bp globally) -> trend short fixed income, ~80% of month's gains
Yields exit a 3.5-5% range after ~4 years of whipsaw; bond vol contained -> vol-scaled signals strengthen
Investor swaps part of 60/40 into trend -> short bonds offsets long bond core; for slow inflation shock, unconstrained medium-term trend is the hedge
mechanisms.fails_when: V-shaped reversals (one a year for four years) and trendless sectors (rates did not trend until Q2 2026)

mechanisms.name: Why VIX-conditioned look-backs are not robust
chain: Rule: faster window in high VIX, slower in low VIX -> results rest on a few activation episodes (about three months of high VIX in the extension)
Long-only equal-notional top-1/top-2 ETF design without vol scaling is relative momentum, not time-series trend
Apparent edge traced to November 2020; none after costs
mechanisms.fails_when: Short-term momentum is stronger at high realised vol, so faster response could matter if deployable in time (Dunne); small samples

playbook.rule: Medium-term trend of roughly a 3-month exponential half-life (not a 3-month window) with a combination of speeds (about 3-12 months; 2-12 month half-lives studied); signal scaled by volatility continuously; scale by signal strength linearly and cap at extremes (sigmoid) while keeping the signal sign.
playbook.why: Matches the SG CTA Trend benchmark; faster speeds lower correlation to 60/40 but cost more; extreme signals are noisy/revert; linear scaling cuts costs

playbook.rule: Do not use VIX/volatility triggers to switch look-backs; use continuous vol scaling; demand the false-positive count for any timing indicator.
playbook.why: Triggers rarely activate; 3 of 33 turning points proves nothing

playbook.rule: Economic trend: directional binary growth/inflation signal, volatility-scaled, long assets that do well in the regime and short the others; complement to price trend (slow, avoids day shocks, would miss equity trend when growth data negative).
playbook.why: Slow regimes avoid daily shocks and add value in corrections

playbook.rule: Carry: bonds from curve slope and roll-down, commodities from neighbouring contracts (seasonality adjusted), currencies from forward basis, equities from futures-implied dividend; standardise as z-score against 1-5 years of own history; run cross-sectionally within asset class; design to minimise spot/trend contribution alongside trend.
playbook.why: Keeps carry relative to normal, cuts beta/principal-component exposure, avoids paying twice for trend

playbook.rule: Cross-sectional commodity carry (strong backwardation) and cross-sectional reversion on realised skewness as diversifiers; curve carry variants: beta-hedge the front, select the back dynamically, or close the spread in backwardation.
playbook.why: Both strong early 2025; hedging the front cut the 2026 loss

playbook.rule: Carry filter on trend: no shorts in positively carrying assets (upward-sloping bond curves) and no longs in negative-carry markets (Longtail Alpha paper, described as sensible but not groundbreaking).
playbook.why: Avoids carry drag pre-2022 while keeping 2022 benefit

playbook.rule: Use the trend signal also as a measure of trendiness to set relative risk across assets; his trend barometer (39 in June 2025) describes the book but is not used as a timing predictor.
playbook.why: Barometer historically does not predict returns except very high readings precede weakness

playbook.rule: Hypotheses only: option-implied skew as a sentiment filter/multiplier on trend; narrative/thematic data as an earlier momentum signal and signal-to-noise gauge; reaction to macro themes conditional on threshold.
playbook.why: Prices/volatilities may be exhausted; V-shapes need a signal-to-noise gauge

playbook.rule: 50-100 markets (10 is cautious; 40-150 look similar at constant vol); choose for diversification and trading cost, not past performance; no screening out of past losers; build medium universes thoughtfully (more ex-US equity indices, more rates tenors); cluster commodities (energy, metals, ags; gas separate from oil), books typically hold 10-40 commodities at about a quarter of risk.
playbook.why: Selecting on performance is data mining; intra-commodity correlation is low

playbook.rule: Core liquid universe if solving for defensiveness/crisis alpha; broader universe including exotic commodities for long-run risk-adjusted return.
playbook.why: Principal components drive crisis returns; independent bets add Sharpe

playbook.rule: Vol-scale every exposure; allocate risk dynamically between asset classes toward where trends exist; scale by volatility and correlation (not volatility only); portfolio vol targeted or bounded so investors can scale next to 60/40.
playbook.why: Fixed budgets embed equal-Sharpe expectations; correlation spikes change dollars needed for a target

playbook.rule: Trend alone at 10-15% volatility; about 20% alongside a strategic allocation (equity-matched); mandates 5-15%; whole portfolio at equity-matching vol (about 15%) is as aggressive as he would go; check historical drawdowns stay below about twice volatility.
playbook.why: Personal risk aversion; a 5% sleeve does little next to 60/40; leverage brings financing constraints

playbook.rule: Considers (no specific rule) a time-varying lower vol target when signal-to-noise is poor; also noted that dynamic vol scaling adds value around V-shaped equity moves; thresholding on weak signals can lag when a move starts from weak signals (July 2026).
playbook.why: Limit leverage into unpredictable turns, manage loss pain without going in or out

playbook.rule: Size a trend allocation by scenario analysis of 2%, 5%, 10%, 15% sleeves against tracking error to the policy portfolio, ideally 5-20% in the strategic benchmark; add trend to stock-bond rather than replacing bonds.
playbook.why: Optimisers give 70%/52%; replacement gives similar or worse long-run portfolio

playbook.rule: Overlay design: for equity-only portfolios limit long-equity risk in the trend overlay; for equity-bond portfolios keep trend unconstrained (inflation shock); if equity beta must be limited cap the position-weighted market-beta sum rather than shorting S&P.
playbook.why: Avoid doubling upside equity risk; both assets fall in inflation shock

playbook.rule: Use expected shortfall not only VaR; monitor correlation dynamics and crowding; design more conservatively than historical data imply; watch gross exposure in crowded momentum; hold equity momentum by volatility-scaling or hedge it fully.
playbook.why: VaR is bounded by history and misses externalities; forced liquidation dominates slippage

playbook.rule: Tolerate the known losing regime rather than alter the models; label one-episode fixes as data mining; treat pain as an invitation to reflect.
playbook.why: Sign of V-shape effect is understood; changes made at the wrong time

playbook.rule: Use cheap options (or zero-DTE as cheap intraday protection) when implied vol is low or for days-to-weeks dips; trend is not for short-lived dips; layer defence options -> trend -> non-short-gamma diversifier.
playbook.why: Trend builds crisis alpha over multi-month paths; options act at once but are costly

playbook.rule: Add beta-neutral carry, reversion and vol selling to trend rather than more beta; run reversion as a separate engine; in trendless regimes do not add parameters to the trend model.
playbook.why: Diversify the periods when trend fails; investors abandon trend in drawdowns

playbook.rule: Dynamic sector tilt toward sectors with positive sector-return trend while keeping full breadth.
playbook.why: Take the opportunity set that delivers conditional on intertemporal trend

playbook.rule: Do not select between trend managers or speeds by recent performance; hold trend as strategic and leave it alone; allocate to defensive strategies by what you are solving for.
playbook.why: Autocorrelation of trend returns doubtful; reactive switching is regret

playbook.rule: Before rebalancing a 60/40 check the trend (do not buy falling equities); avoid month/quarter-end schedules; rebalance frequently with thresholds.
playbook.why: Front-running of scheduled rebalancing; trends persist

playbook.rule: When the macro regime is unclear diversify more and rely less on return-based capital-market assumptions; ~20 portfolio-construction methods with adversarial diversifier is attractive for the construction step (Ang design).
playbook.why: Regime estimate may be wrong

playbook.rule: Rank annual performance of trend speeds (2-12 month half-lives) by universe (concentrated, mid-size, 80+) over 25 years and add the return spread top-bottom; judge designs by turning points and capital preservation.
playbook.why: Show speed/universe interaction by year; ranking alone is incomplete

playbook.rule: Assess a premium by its driver (risk premium vs flow imbalance), capacity and overlap, not just a backtest; retire only if the economic reason changed; monitor aggregate flow and overlap into a premium.
playbook.why: Separates decaying anomalies from durable premia

playbook.rule: Control data mining by culture: call it out, treat tweaks as data mined, justify changes by explaining performance; update a signal's definition (e.g. value) before discarding the idea.
playbook.why: Unavoidable bias; client trust

playbook.rule: Treat speed as one dimension; analyse design features (risk management, sleeves, markets) separately; test alt-data alpha value and decay; verify LLM output; supervised task-specific AI agents inside the deterministic pipeline; point-in-time text data for narrative tests.
playbook.why: Correlation cannot identify behaviour; LLMs err

playbook.rule: In QIS execute passively against guaranteed close/TWAP reference prices market by market; the bank carries slippage so the client gets no execution alpha; close an index that cannot run without impact; design for capacity.
playbook.why: Bank bears execution risk; profitability depends on scale

playbook.rule: Monitor crowding via prime-brokerage net/gross data and trend positions across managers; track a trendiness measure (his firm about the 20th percentile in Apr 2025).
playbook.why: Low trendiness implies reshuffling not crowding

playbook.rule: Build solutions around defined objectives (yield enhancement, flash-correction defence, longer-correction defence) rather than a generic alternatives bucket; use liquid QIS as a liquidity reserve against private-equity capital calls.
playbook.why: Specific outcome focus

evidence_style: Mix of (a) first-principles and algebraic reasoning (PCA, implied returns, leverage arithmetic, loss-aversion, equilibrium/constraint arguments, risk premium vs flow-imbalance), (b) close reading of practitioner and academic papers (Man Group, Quantica, ATP, Graham, AQR, Harvey et al., Penman, Longtail Alpha) reported as reviewer, (c) his own desk data: 25-year speed-by-universe ranking grids, scaled correlations, attribution and trend barometer, and short-window episodes (one week to one month), (d) client/allocator conversations as anecdote. He repeatedly states limits ('I could be wrong', 'I have not tested it', 'my gut feeling', 'I cannot prove'), flags hindsight bias and data mining in his own suggestions, asks for false-positive counts and postmortem data, and rarely shows formal tests on air; several citations are from memory or second-hand.

views_timeline.view: Early-May 2024 trend losses had no common fundamental cause (yield reversal, yen intervention risk, energy dip, cocoa reversal); macro sentiment moved from expected Fed cuts to higher for longer.

US equity momentum led by AI stocks is overcrowded and very hard to time; manage by volatility scaling; unwind could be exogenous (AI enthusiasm fading, value buyers) as well as funding-driven. Cocoa's rally vindicates holding historically poor markets.
views_timeline.reasoning: Record hedge-fund momentum exposure, index concentration, feedback; cocoa a historic negative contributor

views_timeline.view: June 2024 environment not anti-trend (equities trending, VIX near lows); equities the largest 2024 contributor with SG Trend rolling equity beta about 0.4; options are cheap so add hedges.
views_timeline.reasoning: Strong equity trend, benign volatility, VIX near lows

views_timeline.view: August 2024 was a learning week, not an alarm: spike-and-revert is a known cost; trend flipped to long bonds since June; S&P skew at its most attractive in years; alternative commodity trends added almost daily.
views_timeline.reasoning: VIX back at 24; skew repricing; commodity trend insulation

views_timeline.view: After August clients moved from carry-seeking to defensive; no client unwound a trend allocation; FX attribution in a trend program was the worst of any calendar year in 25 years; 60/40 worked as a carry trade plus falling yields and it is open which can persist.
views_timeline.reasoning: Asset owners understand sustained drawdowns, not V-shapes, are where trend pays

views_timeline.view: Carry appetite more conservative after August 2024, vol selling less rewarded in H2; single-stock momentum extremely strong in 2024 but not an obvious crowded unwind; crowding claims against CTAs/QIS unsupported by data.
views_timeline.reasoning: Return numbers vs 10-year range; no data on QIS concentration

views_timeline.view: Barclay CTA AUM near $350bn for ~14 years: adoption flat because investors lack an economic reason that trend should work; 'alternative' is just a tag for something outside the core; replicator can only match underlying CTAs.

Policy uncertainty (tariffs, AI reversals) shifts allocators from carry toward defence; trend flat to slightly positive early 2025 with dollar reversion a detractor while cross-sectional commodity carry and skewness reversion started very strongly; equity-bond correlation may not fall if inflation persists; US yield decline reflects risk aversion but tariffs could push yields up.
views_timeline.reasoning: Allocator conversations; backwardation; inflation-driven positive stock-bond correlation

views_timeline.view: April 2025 was unprecedented-feeling uncertainty (not measurable risk); synchronous V/W-shaped reversions across equities, dollar, oil, yields hit medium-speed trend; no crowded trend position except gold; economic signals (growth falling 2-3 years, inflation undecided) favour gold, bonds, possibly steepeners, no equities.
views_timeline.reasoning: Information in bursts and sentiment-driven moves; prime-brokerage and manager position data

views_timeline.view: April 2025 hit every asset class wrongly positioned; trend remains a crisis hedge and no sustained crisis has occurred; BTOP50 -3.39%, SG CTA -7.6%, SG Trend -10.4% YTD, barometer 39; do not react emotionally but do not be dogmatic.
views_timeline.reasoning: Two reversions in a row; hindsight caveat on any leverage cut

views_timeline.view: Slower beat faster because V-shapes punish fast signals; gold top contributor across an 80+ market universe in 2025 and rates had no trend; beta-neutral carry had one of its best years; a better trend benchmark is a simple bottom-up academic-style model.

QIS $1.3tn figure could be too high (double counting, substitution) or too low; crowding concerns generally overstated but not absent; 2025 trend dispersion mostly speed around the April V-shape (hedged).
2023-25 are the only three consecutive years in 25 where the slowest speed was best, with a small universe first or second; middle speeds worst locally in V-shapes.

2025 possibly one of the largest dispersion years (equities and precious metals won, rates lost); this is a V-shape effect, not evidence for longer trends or small universes; stay reactive and diversified; January 2026 trend about +4-6% at 15% vol, equities then commodities.

March 2026: oil/gas backwardation hit commodity curve carry; trend (vol-scaled) flat with oil and short rates positive and equities hurt; faster speeds outperformed; stagflation risk higher; environment of fundamental certainty brought reversions (caption garbled).
views_timeline.reasoning: Own book results; oil shock lifts inflation nowcasts

views_timeline.view: Inflation is the central theme of 2026 (sticky inflation could change stock-bond correlation); March 2026 V was unusual (slow drop, fast recovery) and hurt defensive products; commodity curve carry not broken (known risk, worst drawdown in 40 years); trend benefiting from broad contribution; WSJ QIS-crowding charge is a textbook point.
views_timeline.reasoning: Premium logic; Hormuz disruption; YTD attribution

views_timeline.view: 2026 is a good year for trend and diversifiers (up five of seven months if July positive; March and June losers); carry strong in FX and commodities on backwardation; client interest in trend and diversifiers rising; July 2026 equity and bond both fell and trend gained 0.9-1.3%.
views_timeline.reasoning: Rates shorts and commodities drove July; equity reversals caused losses

views_timeline.view: September 2026 strong trend month driven by short bonds (about 80% of gains); 2026 third-best trend year in 15; no strong view on why yields are rising (Jan-Feb easing consensus was wrong); equity breadth deteriorating (45% negative-beta stocks) implies dispersion; not changing his trend model on VIX-look-back evidence.
views_timeline.reasoning: Managers' attribution; Goldman chart; Alpha Architect test

how_views_changed: Core framework is stable across 2024-09/2026: V-shapes hurt trend (especially the middle speeds), do not change models after pain, trend is strategic and untimed, diversify with carry/reversion, vol-scale. Changes are in emphasis, not reversals, and are mostly tied to market events rather than to explained revisions. (1) Sizing: May-Aug 2024 he personally prefers dynamic vol scaling and dynamic asset-class allocation (MT117-C09-1, MT099-C08-R3); Oct 2024 he says static and dynamic converge long-run and matter at turning points (MT200-C10-2); June 2025 he floats a lower/time-varying vol target after repeated V-shapes but flags hindsight (MT087-C08-2, MT087-C08-X1); Jan 2026 he is 'reactive and diversified by design' and does not claim it was wrong though it cost performance (MT116-C08-1). (2) Speed/universe: Aug 2024 'neither speed better' (MT099-C10-3); Dec 2025/Jan 2026 slow and small-universe won 2023-25 but due to V-shapes (MT134-C03-4, MT116-C08-2); Mar 2026 faster speeds won (MT167-C06-1); Jul 2026 prefer slower for defence, objective decides universe (MT174-C09-X1, MT174-C06-2). (3) AI: mid-2025 an LLM fabricated ten references (MT087-C02-1); Mar-Jul 2026 supervised agents and a daily agent with checks (MT167-C14-X10, MT174-C03-2). (4) Sector emphasis moved from equity-led 2024, to gold/no rates trend 2025, to rates and inflation 2026 (MT009-C04-1, MT130-C03-1). He gives market reasons for these shifts but never states that he revised a belief ('not explained' as a self-revision).

disagreements.their_position: Diversifying components (carry, reversion, agnostic risk parity) can enhance trend; concentrating on the dominant trend component has diminishing value, but avoids grossed-up spreads.
disagreements.other_position: Prefers pure trend; anything else is 'trend minus' and may cannibalise.

disagreements.their_position: Open to a dynamic lower vol target when signal-to-noise is low, with hindsight and path-dependency caveats; dynamic matters locally, converges long-run.
disagreements.other_position: His firm has used dynamic risk budgeting 12+ years; some managers let vol swing 30 to 90 which he finds wild; static vs dynamic long-run returns hard to tell apart.

disagreements.their_position: Mathematically a return maximiser holds near 100% (about 70% MV, 52% downside); no single optimum because of tracking-error and career risk.
disagreements.other_position: Surprised at 100%; 70-80 might already be unrealistic; clients accept far less than consultants imply.

disagreements.their_position: Narrative and thematic data might lead price; dealer gamma matters for short-term trend and implied skew might be a sentiment filter.
disagreements.other_position: Doubles down on price-only trend with no story; option volume is irrelevant to 3-24 month trends; themes may be marketing.

disagreements.their_position: Narratives lift prices only while demand lasts, which needs anticipated performance; if value fails the definition may be outdated.
disagreements.other_position: Price and value have broken apart; narratives and speculation dominate, so price-only is the strength.

disagreements.their_position: Tilt dynamically to sectors that deliver, conditional on sector-return trend.
disagreements.other_position: Full diversification across the whole breadth is more intuitive; small universes were worst for ~7 years after the tech bubble.

disagreements.topic: Did CTAs slow? what is a trend benchmark
disagreements.their_position: Correlation shifts do not prove speed change; SG Trend Index is beta plus alpha, use simple bottom-up academic model.
disagreements.other_position: Long-term signals with agile risk management can look short-term; SG Trend Indicator tracks daily trend well.

disagreements.topic: Short-term vs medium-term speed; shock flips
disagreements.their_position: Neither speed better in general: depends on true/false positive; depending on speed a fraction or most markets turned.
disagreements.other_position: Short-term trend works less well; a few-day shock cannot flip medium/long positions.

disagreements.their_position: Broader because large reversions make design matter and managers differentiated after 2022; depends on manager set.
disagreements.other_position: CFM finds no more dispersion than historically.

disagreements.their_position: Contagion comes from simultaneous losses and synchronous unwinding, not the measure; crowded positions matter more.
disagreements.other_position: Worries many managers moving from stop losses to VaR synchronise forced selling.

disagreements.their_position: Vol only as continuous scaling and risk budgeting; regime timing unproven; deploying speed dynamically is the open question.
disagreements.other_position: Some managers trade faster in high vol and short-term momentum is stronger at high realised vol; vintage-restricted models may be too weak for agent backtests.

disagreements.topic: Execution value in QIS vs CTA; broad vs concentrated universe in 2026
disagreements.their_position: No execution alpha for the client in a QIS; core for defensiveness, broad for long-run Sharpe, one year does not decide.
disagreements.other_position: In a CTA slippage flows to the client so execution research matters; concentrated metals/energy CTAs up 50-100% but hindsight.

disagreements.with: Katy Kaminski / Andrew Beer / Cem Karsan / panel
disagreements.their_position: Dispersion from speed, universe, purity; crowding concerns overstated; locally middle speeds worst, year on year slower better in 2023-25.
disagreements.other_position: Beer: not meaningfully larger; Karsan: compression builds potential energy; Beer: slowness helped, Kaminski: 6-8 month mid-range overreacted most.

disagreements.topic: When to change a model / judge managers by statistics
disagreements.their_position: Change or retire only when the underlying premium changes; pain invites review of blind spots, not change.
disagreements.other_position: Beer: almost never; Gitt: only if market properties change or measured breakdown; Dunne: 10+ years needed; Carver: 75% confidence is acceptable.

internal_tensions.issue: Static vs dynamic: he personally prefers dynamic vol scaling and dynamic risk allocation across asset classes (MT099-C08-2, MT117-C09-1) and dynamic sector tilting (MT116-C09-2), yet says trend must be a strategic never-timed allocation (MT087-C14-1), long-run static and dynamic converge (MT200-C10-2), and that using static sizing for August 2024 would be data mining (MT200-C07-1).

Do-not-change-models vs openness to design change: refuses refits after one event (MT002-C02-5b, MT221-C08-2, MT200-C05-1) but floats a lower vol target because V-shapes are more frequent (MT087-C08-2) and notes V-shapes recur about once a year for four years (MT009-C09-2), and says clients' interest in 'reactive' design is legitimate; also notes his reactive, diversified mindset cost performance recently (MT116-C07-R1).

Crowding: says crowding cannot be timed and blame on CTAs/QIS/vol targeters is unsupported (MT002-C06-4, MT099-C14-2, MT130-C05-2), yet describes crowded momentum as a party with a liquidity hangover (MT117-C14-2), asks to design more conservatively because externalities are unquantifiable (MT216-C03-3), and that QIS wrapper crowding hurt intraday momentum in 2021-22 (MT204-C15-3).

Forecasting: says even identifying the current state is hard and returns are not forecastable (MT009-C03-1, MT200-C09-2), yet regime-maps growth/inflation to gold, bonds, no equities (MT039-C15-4, MT087-C16-2) and reads 2026 as inflation-centred with stock-bond correlation at stake (MT130-C03-1).

Regime/trendiness timing: trend strength does not predict performance and VIX timing is unproven (MT087-C09-3, MT009-C08-X1), yet he uses trendiness to set relative risk across assets (MT131-C07-X6) and explores option skew and narrative intensity as conditional signal-to-noise gauges (MT167-C10-2, MT116-C03-2).

Pure trend vs trend-plus: says relative-value spreads from small signal differences are arguably not trend (MT117-C06-2) and prefers pure direction, but advocates carry/reversion/ARP sleeves as part of the multi-strategy pitch (MT117-C07-X1, MT174-C05-1) and says he is a fan for two to three years (MT174-C05-1).
Speed: argues no speed is best (MT099-C10-3, MT200-C05-1) yet backs slower trend for defence (MT174-C09-X1) and cites 2023-25 slow winners (MT134-C03-4); March 2026 faster won (MT167-C06-1).

Equity exposure: trend should be left unconstrained on equities to keep timing skill and bull participation (MT173-C08-3) vs reduce long-equity risk in the overlay for equity-only portfolios (MT174-C09-2); both are tied to objective but the first is stated for trend programs, the second for overlays.
Reported QIS size is stated as USD 600-700bn (MT167-C02-3) and later as uncertain around $1.3tn, with a broker-dealer $600bn +/-100bn guess (MT204-C05-2).

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: In V-shaped equity/macro reversals, medium trend speeds (3-6 month) have worse drawdown than both fast (1-2 month) and slow (12 month) speeds; over sustained-drawdown years all speeds profit and ranking of speeds matters little.
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: Daily futures returns across 50-100 markets 1999+; trend signals at 1/3/6/12-month half-lives; define V-events by drawdown and recovery within N days; compare speed P&L

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: Trend returns in the three months before an equity peak and the first weeks of a drawdown are insignificant; they appear only once the drawdown is sustained (dotcom, GFC, 2022).
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: S&P peak dates, trend index or replicated trend daily returns, event-time averages

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: Trendiness (barometer) does not predict next-period trend returns except that very high trendiness precedes underperformance.
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: Cross-sectional and time-series trendiness measure (e.g. share of variance in first principal component of signals), forward 1-12 month returns

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: Dynamic risk allocation toward trending asset classes (vs 25% each equal risk) raises long-run return but increases loss in equity reversals; long-run static and dynamic converge, local difference at turning points.
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: Asset-class level trend backtests with balanced vs trendiness-weighted risk; event study of Aug 2024, Mar 2023, Apr 2025

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: Scaling trend positions linearly with signal strength and flattening/capping at extreme signals (sigmoid) beats binary and linear after costs, because extreme signals revert.
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: Futures panel; compare binary/linear/sigmoid transfer functions net of costs, per asset class

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: Dispersion of trend programs in a year is driven more by lookback speed and universe breadth than by sizing method (dynamic vs static, correlation use) when vols and correlations are stable (stated as untested hunch).
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: Grid of speed x universe x sizing rules, annual return dispersion decomposition

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: A core liquid universe (equity, duration) maximises crisis alpha and cash efficiency, while a broad 50-100+ universe maximises long-run Sharpe; beyond 70-80 liquid macro markets nothing is added, exotic commodities still add return.
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: Marginal Sharpe and crisis-quarter contribution as markets are added in liquidity order; principal-component exposure

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: Capping equity beta in a trend program improves the worst S&P quarters by about 40-50bp but costs about 200bp a year long-run; capping market-beta-weighted exposure beats shorting S&P futures.
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: Trend program with equity cap variants; worst-quarter and full-sample returns

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: Beta-neutral carry and reversion added to trend diversify the periods when trend fails (V-shapes) without lowering correlation profile; carry z-scored against 1-5 years of own history and designed with minimal spot contribution beats raw carry alongside trend.
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: Cross-sectional and time-series carry, reversion on realised skew, combined with trend; period splits around V-events

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: Commodity curve carry (long back, short front) mean-reverts after backwardation shocks and shows no visible decay over 15 years; beta-hedging the front or closing the spread in backwardation cuts the drawdown.
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: Commodity futures term structure; variants of curve carry; shock episodes 2018, 2026

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: Under fundamental uncertainty (disputed valuation, inflation volatility) trend performs; under fundamental certainty (Fed put era) prices revert and trend is weaker.
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: Proxy for dispersion of views / inflation uncertainty (survey dispersion, policy uncertainty), trend returns by regime

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: Stocks exposed to rising narratives outperform those exposed to fading narratives, with a signal distinct from price momentum, and rising narratives lead price momentum.
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: Point-in-time article data (e.g. 13.3m articles, 347 narratives or 30-60 evergreen topics), narrative betas, forward returns controlling for momentum

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: Front-running of calendar rebalancing (60/40 month/quarter-end) costs about 8bp a year; rebalancing frequently with thresholds, or checking trend before rebalancing, reduces cost.
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: Stock-bond rebalance flow estimates, fast-money positioning around month/quarter ends

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: A defensive trend overlay should be unconstrained for equity-bond portfolios (inflation shock hurts both) and long-equity-limited for equity-only portfolios.
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: Overlay simulations on 60/40 and equity-only; worst inflation-shock quarters; tracking error

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: Rates and sector contribution to trend rotates (rates top for 20 years, failing after 2022); tilting toward sectors with positive sector-return trend improves the book vs static breadth.
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: Sector contribution series, sector-trend tilt overlay with costs

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: Dealer long gamma (zero-DTE) induces intraday mean reversion that mainly drags short-term trend, little effect on medium or long-term trend.
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: Intraday futures data, zero-DTE share, dealer gamma estimates, short-term trend index returns

testable_hypotheses.hypothesis: Loss-averse allocators who keep a non-trend component (carry, reversion) stay allocated through trend drawdowns and so realise higher long-run trend returns.
testable_hypotheses.data_needed: Allocator flow data around trend drawdowns by strategy composition

blind_spots: (reader) Rarely gives a quantitative cost or expected-return number for trend or carry premia, and almost no own live performance except qualitative or short-window figures; most evidence is episodes (Aug 2024, Apr 2025, Mar 2026) rather than long-sample tests.
(reader) Says dynamic risk allocation and dynamic vol scaling are better locally yet gives no backtest comparing fixed and dynamic budgets (MT117 evidence is algebra and 2022 hindsight).

(reader) No explicit account of why V-shaped reversals have become more frequent (political/policy regime, information bursts, option flows are offered but not tested); unclear whether recurring V-shapes will persist.

(reader) Takes no fundamental valuation or earnings view; no view on equities, credit or FX beyond trend/carry/reversion signals; rarely addresses stock selection or sector valuation except momentum and themes.

(reader) Does not quantify capacity or transaction costs of trend beyond naming them, nor decay of trend returns after QIS/CTA inflows beyond assertion; crowding of trend is argued from premium type, not data.
(reader) Theme/narrative claims are second-hand from papers he did not write (MT174), with no tested result of his own.
(reader) Statements on peers' behaviour (CTA research mostly changes risk management, not speed) are assumptions he flags as possibly wrong (MT131-C06-1).
(reader) Never addresses fiscal dominance, debt cycles, or long-run valuation; policy matters only as a source of shocks/uncertainty.
reader_inferences: (reader) Identity/role labels differ across episodes: caption names include 'Nick Palus' (MT009), 'Nick Balters' (MT134, MT204), 'Nick Bolas/Bolters' (MT099, MT131, MT117), and employer is guessed as Goldman Sachs (MT009, MT130, MT204, MT174), Man Group (MT167) or a generic bank/QIS group; the pack's speaker blocks were attributed to one person by the map pipeline. MT009 ('Nick Palus', Sept 2026) carries the greatest identity doubt; its content (volatility-scaled trend, V-shapes, false positives, QIS/index design) matches the rest, so it is included.

(reader) His worldview is a 'robustness over cleverness' stance: preferred actions are those that leave the design unchanged (breadth, vol-scaling, diversification with carry/reversion, strategic sizing) and unpreferred are any rules fitted to the last drawdown; this explains why he repeatedly attacks recency while himself running dynamic risk allocation.

(reader) A possible testable synthesis: the persistent elements are (1) volatility-scaled multi-speed trend on 50-100 markets, (2) dynamic risk budget following trendiness with correlation, (3) beta-neutral carry and reversion sleeves, (4) objective-specific universe (core vs broad), (5) no screening on past performance, (6) allocation sized by tracking error; a benchmark replicator based on these would be a reasonable test of his claims.

(reader) His main failure condition is a persistent environment of V-shaped reversals plus fundamental certainty (Fed put), which he calls the weak decade for trend (2010s), and he expects trend to do well under inflation volatility and policy uncertainty (2022, 2026); that is a regime map that could be tested with inflation/policy-uncertainty data.
(reader) Several statements about his own book (barometer, speed grids, attribution) are not independently verifiable from the transcript; treat them as stated, not checked.
